headings.note: Chapters are marked with h4 or h5 inconsistently (Chapters I to IV and VI are h5; V and VII to XI are h4); front matter, epilogue, counsels, letters, prayers, and poems also use h4/h5.

survey.verse:
No verse markup or classes. Poems and quoted verse are paragraphs whose lines end in
(about 49 such passages, besides 7 list-like paragraphs); line breaks only, no stanza or indent information.
survey.notes: No note markup. 611 bracketed note markers such as [1] appear as plain text, the same 611 as in the TXT; note texts are plain paragraphs at the end of each chapter. The transcriber's note in both files says footnotes were renumbered and a few modified or omitted.
survey.wordAlignmentWithTxt: 107,466 words in each. Every word matches once accents are folded: the HTML drops accents and ligatures that the TXT keeps (Therese for Thérèse, Ame for Âme, anaemia for anæmia, haemorrhage for hæmorrhage). Difflib ratio 0.9966 before folding.

assessment: Richer than #130 for Orthodoxy: italics and line-broken verse are present, but notes are plain text and heading levels are inconsistent. Structure (headings, paragraphs, verse line breaks) could be taken from it with an accent-folding alignment rule; italics would need a decision, since the TXT already carries most of them as underscores. Survey only; not built.
use: Survey for the structured-text pilot (Part C). Original bytes retained unchanged; Gutenberg license and credits included.
storage: Original HTML bytes stored gzip-compressed (deterministic: mtime 0, no stored filename) so the repository does not publish them as untagged site pages. sha256 and bytes describe the decompressed original; gzipSha256 describes the stored file.
